column1: # Claims this project has RETRACTED. A retired claim must not reappear in any live page or in the tools.
# Why a gate and not care: the hard-link claim below was reported corrected twice and was still on ELEVEN
# live pages and inside forefst.py -- including printed output -- when a third review found it. No existing
# check could see it: check_doc_drift compares sentences for NUMERIC disagreement (this claim has no
# numbers) and check_doc_vocabulary is scoped to retired output tokens INSIDE FENCED CODE BLOCKS.
#   pattern   Python regex, matched case-insensitively against text with hard wraps joined
#   unless    regex that, if found in the SAME sentence, means the text is stating the correction
#   retired_by  the measurement that retracted it
#   correct   one line: what to say instead

column5: correct

A SetFileTime through one hard-link name updates the FILE'S OWN RECORD for every name at once; each name's index entry is a cache the driver refreshes only for the name that was opened, so divergence is evidence, agreement clears nothing (a read produces it too), and which name is authentic is not established.
Do not name an authentic birth from the sibling set; the mechanism behind the observed divergence was never decompiled.
The tool flags EVERY name of a diverging group; flagging only one would assert the others are clean.

A name-scoped SetFileTime updates the FILE'S OWN RECORD for every name at once, so it is not itself the cause of a divergence. What diverges is each NAME'S INDEX ENTRY, a lazily refreshed cache: RefsUpdateFileDupInfo refreshes only the opened name's entry, so an un-opened sibling keeps pre-stomp times and any read erases them. Divergence is evidence; agreement clears nothing; which name is authentic is still not established.
A sparse hole is identified by flags bit 0x20; a hole's VLCN mirrors its file VCN and is usually non-zero. VLCN 0 is only a read-time floor.
A checksummed extent carries one CRC-32C per cluster and declares it in record size (24 + run*4); 0x1C00D0 is flags 0x00D0 with record size 28, i.e. run == 1 only.
A redo block's record budget is its own total_size; first_record_offset only locates the first record.
The last record of a redo block carries the commit flag (bit 1 at +0x2C) on every block measured.
Bytes per sector is 512 on a 512e volume and 4096 on a 4Kn one; total_sectors counts sectors of that size.
The carves 1.13.0 refused were genuine: 86 of 93 with a live twin are byte-identical to it. The cause was a prior row version marking runs unwritten, and an unaligned row step.
The runs summed to exactly `needed` because the rows are real; extent rows are 8-byte aligned and 1.13.0 stepped by the unaligned size.
GFSAREPLAY / GFSAPPEND are the test generator's own content markers, not filesystem metadata.

Opcodes 0x12 and 0x15 call no handler in PerformRedo (17134, 26100.x, Insider 29574); only 0x14 calls RedoMoveContainer. 0x12 is a tree-update record, read by the analysis pass (TreeUpdateRecordFound).
timestomp has no FUTURE signal: it compared Created with $VOLUME_INFORMATION+0xA0, the volume modify time (updated on mount), not a last metadata write; MEDIUM is CHANGE_LATE without PRE_FORMAT.
$VOLUME_INFORMATION+0xA0 is the volume modify time, updated on mount; no field read here is the volume's last metadata write.
refs.sys sets the commit flag (bit 1 at +0x2C) on the last record of each transaction; on the volumes measured the last record of every redo block carries it.
A creation time LATER than a snapshot of the same file is impossible; one below it is the normal order, so backdating is not caught by a snapshot.
Say what the journal shows: its surviving records end at USN X while files still point past it; the journal cannot tell whether those records were lost or removed.
An allocated all-zero $J that no file points into is a note (exit 0); it is a finding only when files point into it, and the finding names them.
An image hole is stated as a hole with its cause left open: not captured, or zero on the disk; the image cannot tell which.
State the measured figure with its set: 886,932 data records and the 248 control copies of the 124 corpus volumes recompute (2026-11-09).
`timeline` merges the USN, MLog and $SI rows and sorts them by time; rows are not joined across sources.

_SmsRedoRecord+0x20 is the volume's allocator clock when the record was added (AddRedoRecord; the checkpoint's +0x68 holds the same clock); the object id is in the record's key (component 0), where ObjectIdFromRedoHelper reads it.
A `mlog --parse` row is one log payload, which can merge up to 15 transactions (`Log payloads: N (M transaction starts)`).
IsResident was removed in 1.14.0; DataResidency `inline` says the same.
MLog control area: +0x18 Log start, +0x20 Log end (as of the last control-area write), +0x38 Log open count (u32).

Checkpoint flag 0x400 is not a CRC64 / verification switch (E141): it marks the record's rollback-protection fields, +0x9C offset / +0xA0 length, set by refs.sys on a volume of version 3.13 or later (E158).
What refs.sys does with checkpoint flag 0x400 is read (E158): FormatCheckpointRecord sets it under VersionCheck(0x30d); it marks the rollback-protection fields +0x9C / +0xA0.
Claims are checked against two independent sources, the driver's code and the bytes on disk, wherever both can be read; the register records which of the two supports each claim.
Some register rows record a single image as their disk witness; the register gives each row's evidence.

The references of a v3.4 volume declare CRC64 (156 of 156 root references), and the 17134 driver checks a page it reads from disk against its reference.
A checksum that recomputes shows a page holds what the volume recorded; the checksums are not keyed, so it does not prove nobody edited the page.
Every format's page references carry CRC64 (or SHA-256) and the 3.4 driver checks a page against its reference; 3.10 added the selector at VBR 0x2A, not verification.
Hard-link support is the boot-sector flag 0x20, set at format time from 3.7; a volume upgraded from 3.4 has none.
A file's 128-bit reference is its creation directory's OID (frozen across rename and move) and its ordinal in that directory; files have no OID of their own.
the format coverage is ReFS 3.4-3.14; 3.15 is a preview driver's maximum and its stamp, not a volume format

RefsLinkFileToSelf runs once per file: it re-parents the file's own table under the type-0x40 key {0x80000040, 0, file reference} (0x80000040 is the key prefix, not a tag) and writes back only the name the record sat under; each further name is written by RefsAddLink from RefsSetLinkInfo.
0x2A and 0x48 are the format-time fields; the volume flags at 0x2C are written at run time (a writable mount sets 0x02, among others), and only their bits 0x20 and 0x40 come from the format

column5: A schema id names a table (a file's record, a directory's own row, a data stream, a system table) chosen by the format era; an attribute has no schema of its own.
0x1E0 is the schema of a file's record table on formats 3.11 and later, not of $EA.
0x1B0 is a registered schema with a file-table shape whose role is not read; stream snapshots are type-0xB0 rows.
0x1F0 is the schema of a directory's own-row table on formats 3.11 and later; $Max is the type-0xF0 attribute.

A record's first 40 bytes are its table's _SmsIndexRoot descriptor: node offset, size, flags, schema id, checksum type, integrity, leaf pages, row count.
The driver's attribute table names type 0x50 $OBSOLETE and 0x70 $VOLUME_INFORMATION; the volume information is rows of the table at OID 0x500 (schema 0x150).
The driver's attribute table names type 0x60 $VOLUME_NAME; the reparse index is the system table at OID 0x540 (schema 0x160).
OID 0x530 is a B+-tree table of schema 0x140.
The checkpoint's 32-byte area is the change journal's cursor {FirstUsn, NextUsn, wrap base, wrap size}.
Boot-sector flag 0x04 selects the volume's schema set (17134: 0x180 set vs the older 0x110 set; 26100 refuses below 3.6 without it).
